Wholesale and bulk

Shop by category

This category holds one product, NAD+, and NAD+ is not a peptide, as the questions below explain. On FDA's list of bulk substances nominated for 503A compounding, updated May 14, 2026, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) is in Category 1, the substances FDA is still evaluating.1 In October 2024, FDA said it was aware of compounders making intravenous products from food-grade NAD+ sold by repackagers.3 It reported adverse events after NAD+ injectable drugs, including severe chills, shaking, vomiting and fatigue, some needing medical treatment, and said those reactions are consistent with excessive endotoxins.4

The cognitive goal guide maps what published studies report, compound by compound, with evidence levels.

Frequently asked questions

Where can I purchase injectable NAD?

Not here as an injectable medicine. NAD+ is sold as a 500 mg vial labeled for research use only, and NAD+ is not an FDA-approved drug in the US.56 Health Canada's April 2026 warning about injectable peptides bought online named NAD+ among unauthorized products.7 For lab work, mixing and storage are covered on the NAD+ reconstitution page, and the vial itself is on the NAD+ product page.

Is NAD+ a peptide?

No. Its full name, as FDA's compounding list gives it, is nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide.1 That makes it a dinucleotide, while NHGRI defines a peptide as a short chain of amino acids, typically 2 to 50, joined by peptide bonds.2 It is sold in this shop next to the peptides and filed in this category by the catalog. The NAD+ education page covers what published research reports about it.

Is Semax in this category?

No. Semax is sold here but filed under no category, and Selank sits under sleep and stress. FDA's advisory committee reviewed semax in July 2026 for cerebral ischemia, migraine and trigeminal neuralgia.8 Trade press reported a narrow vote recommending it for the 503A bulks list; FDA must still act and go through rulemaking.9 FDA says it has no or limited safety information on semax for the proposed routes, and lacks important information on any safety issues when selank acetate is given to people.10
